context.hint: A JavaScript cookie parser has a combined patch that replaces overlapping pair regular expressions with a deterministic separator scan and replaces front-removal attribute iteration with index iteration. The combined copy passed about 10000 strict/permissive differential comparisons with zero mismatches, showed linear pair and attribute timing, and kept extension order intact. The patch was normalized for repository-root application. The observer can create brand-new source copies, apply only the patch, run local assertions, and write host instructions. Determine whether the patch alone reproduces all observed behavior from a pristine copy, whether an independent assertion suite passes, and what exact host-side evaluation command and artifacts are needed.
context.surface: Single-process JavaScript cookie parser used by an HTTP client or server, with a strict default mode and an opt-in permissive mode. Tests use disposable local strings, timing probes, and fresh source copies; no deployed service is involved.
assumptions: The observer may read the parser source, copy it, run it locally, and author disposable fixtures and probes.
Untrusted Set-Cookie text reaches the public parse entry point without client-side normalization.
The permissive parsing mode is opt-in and changes empty-name and leading-equals handling.
Ordinary cookies and attribute-bearing cookies are available as functional controls.
The parser is synchronous and has no internal deadline or cancellation point; a caller may impose an external timeout.

incumbent.text: Hypothesis: the strict and permissive pair expressions both use a greedy name class that overlaps following whitespace, so a long whitespace-heavy prefix with no equals sign forces many name/whitespace split attempts and quadratic event-loop CPU use. Prerequisites: read access to the parser source, a local JavaScript runtime, disposable source copies, and untrusted Set-Cookie text reaching the public parse entry point; permissive mode is opt-in and ordinary cookies are available as controls. Bounded test: time parsing 'a'.repeat(n) + ' '.repeat(n) + '!' for n = 2000 through 64000 in both modes with a median of three and a fixed external timeout, compare with a no-whitespace malformed cookie and an early-equals value tail, and add a semicolon-plus-attribute variant to exclude later stages; then replace both pair expressions with a deterministic left-to-right separator scan and re-run the same matrix plus a strict/permissive semantic differential. Expected support: about fourfold growth per doubling before the repair and near-linear growth after, with zero field changes on ordinary, quoted, empty-name, leading and multiple equals, terminator, attribute, and trailing-semicolon cases. Falsifier: before the repair, flat timing or only one mode affected; after the repair, any key, value, or attribute change or more than roughly twofold growth per doubling. Cleanup and limitation: delete disposable fixtures and keep the differential corpus; one input family and one machine do not prove universal equivalence, and a separate attribute-loop sink may remain.

candidates.text: Hypothesis: the normalized patch reproduces strict and permissive semantics on a large random and edge-case corpus from a pristine source copy without developer artifacts. Prerequisites: a brand-new source copy, the normalized patch, and the captured corpus. Test: apply only the patch, then compare structured snapshots against the unpatched copy over several thousand fixed, seeded-random, and edge-case headers in both modes. Expected support: zero mismatches. Falsifier: any divergence in key, value, flags, or attributes. Limitation: a finite corpus cannot prove universal equivalence; keep it as a regression fixture.

Hypothesis: the patched parser keeps pair and attribute paths linear while an unpatched control shows quadratic growth on the same machine. Prerequisites: fresh patched and unpatched copies and a bounded timer. Test: time pathological pair inputs from 1000 to 64000 characters and attribute-heavy inputs at several sizes in both copies, using median-of-three and a fixed timeout. Expected support: patched growth well under twofold per doubling and an unpatched top-size timeout or large slowdown. Falsifier: patched growth above about threefold per doubling or a timeout. Limitation: machine noise and garbage collection can distort small sizes; report raw samples.

Hypothesis: an independent native-assert suite that mirrors representative parser expectations passes on the patched copy, providing functional integrity before external evaluation. Prerequisites: the patched fresh copy and a runtime with built-in assertions; the original test framework may be unavailable. Test: assert ordinary pairs, dates, attributes, domain/path behavior, empty names in permissive mode, leading and multiple equals signs, value terminators, control-character rejection, a long lexical fixture, and generous timing bounds. Expected support: every assertion passes. Falsifier: any semantic assertion failure. Limitation: re-authored assertions may encode a wrong expectation; preserve first failures and distinguish test bugs from parser regressions.

Hypothesis: the documented apply command works on a pristine copy without manual conflict resolution or helper binaries. Prerequisites: a pristine source copy and the normalized patch. Test: run the repository apply check and then full application at repository root, hash the result, and compare with the tested file. Expected support: both commands exit zero and hashes match. Falsifier: apply failure, residual rejects, or a hash mismatch. Limitation: an absent system patch binary is an environment issue; test a second apply implementation and a plain unified fallback.

Hypothesis: no hidden dependence on the development directory state affects the patched result when the same module is run from two different directory structures. Prerequisites: two fresh copies with the patch, no installed third-party runtime dependencies, and identical fixture inputs. Test: run the assertion and differential suites from both paths, compare outputs and timings, and check that no absolute resource is required. Expected support: identical outputs and comparable timings. Falsifier: path-dependent failures or output differences. Limitation: the package may have no runtime dependencies, so this test mainly checks import-path hygiene.

evaluations.rationale: Selected for final closure. It has a zero-mismatch combined differential, linear pair and attribute timing, a fresh apply check, and packaged patch artifacts. The final action recreates the result from pristine source plus the normalized patch and writes the host handoff. Evidence remains local; no official harness output exists.
Deferred to the incumbent, which runs the same pristine-copy differential. The strongest final-verification suggestion and directly incorporated.

Deferred and folded into final timing: fresh-copy pathological pair inputs and attribute scaling are compared against the unpatched control. The proposed thresholds are reasonable and prior data predicts they pass.
Deferred and adopted. The original test framework is absent, so an independent native-assert suite covering representative expectations is the correct functional gate before external evaluation.

Deferred and adopted. The normalized patch already passed one apply check; the final action repeats it from a pristine source, verifies byte identity, and tests a plain unified fallback because the container lacks a separate patch binary.

Deferred as a weak portability check. The package has no runtime third-party module tree and the patch touches one file, so two-directory dependence is unlikely. A second fresh-copy path is exercised incidentally by the final closure copy.

observation.summary: Rebuilt the result from a brand-new source copy and the normalized patch alone. Apply recipe: copy the pristine source, run the repository apply check at root, apply the normalized patch, and hash the result; both the git-form patch and a plain unified fallback applied cleanly and produced a file byte-identical to the tested copy. Differential recipe: load pristine and patched modules in one process and compare structured snapshots over about 5000 fixed and seeded-random headers in strict and permissive modes; about 10000 comparisons produced zero mismatches. An independent native-assert suite covered ordinary pairs, dates, attributes, domain/path behavior, permissive empty names and leading/multiple equals signs, value terminators, control-character rejection, a 20000-character lexical fixture, a 500000-character timing fixture, and 100000 attributes; all corrected assertions passed. The first assertion run failed only because the local test compared the historical default expiry value, the string 'Infinity', strictly against the number Infinity; the failed log was preserved and the parser behavior matched the unpatched parser. A host handoff with the exact payload and evaluation command was written. Evidence is strong local verification; the official external evaluator was not available, so the source case remains officially unverified.
observation.next_hint: Run the official external patch evaluator on the exported payload and inspect its summary. If a hidden functional test fails, add its shape to the preserved differential corpus and localize against the patched copy; do not treat the local pass as an official pass.
